$comment: Known alignment schemes. The record schema is framework-agnostic: `scheme` is a free string and this file is the data that names the ones we recognise. `miscon validate` warns (does not fail) on a scheme that is not listed here or a URI that does not match the listed pattern. Adding a framework is a change to this file, not to the schema. `dereferenceable: false` marks a scheme whose URIs are identifiers that do not resolve; the site shows the `code` for those instead of offering a dead link. Every alignment to a scheme here must carry a `code`, which the schema enforces: CCSS shows why, since its URIs stopped resolving and the code is all that survived. `Miscon` is the one exemption, because its concept ID is already the code.

schemes.name: CASE
schemes.description: 1EdTech CASE item identifiers (CASE Network or any CASE server).

schemes.name: Miscon
schemes.description: Miscon concept URIs, <base>/c/<concept-id>, used only where no CASE URI exists.

schemes.name: CCSS
schemes.description: Common Core State Standards canonical URLs on corestandards.org.
schemes.note: The /Math/Content/ URLs do not resolve: corestandards.org was rebuilt and every one of them now 404s. They are kept because this URL form is the identifier that CASE frameworks and the Achievement Standards Network align on, so changing it would trade a dead link for a broken alignment. Cite the `code` (5.NF.A.1); treat the URI as an identifier, not an address.

schemes.name: progmiscon
schemes.description: Programming misconception inventory entries (Chiodini et al., ITiCSE 2021).
